title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
summary: Each flight row gives a departure city, an arrival city, and a price.

contractDetails.constraints: 2–100 cities labeled from 0. Up to n(n−1)/2 flights, with different endpoints, distinct ordered endpoint pairs, and integer prices in [1, 10000]. src and dst differ. 0 ≤ k < n.

statement: Each flight row gives a departure city, an arrival city, and a price. Find the cheapest route from src to dst with at most k intermediate stops. Return −1 if no such route exists.

examples.explanation: The cheaper three-flight route has two stops and exceeds this limit.
With two stops, all three flights fit and cost 9.

constraints: 2–100 cities labeled from 0. Up to n(n−1)/2 flights, with different endpoints, distinct ordered endpoint pairs, and integer prices in [1, 10000]. src and dst differ. 0 ≤ k < n.
hints: Conceptual: A route with k stops uses at most k + 1 flights.
Directional: Track cheapest prices after each permitted flight count.
Implementation: Relax from a snapshot of the previous round so a single round cannot chain several flights.
complexityAnalysis: O((k + 1)(V + E)) time and O(V) auxiliary space using two cost arrays.
